answer: subnet token buckets cap distinct identities by hashing each registration to a shared rate-limit pool, so a sybil cluster drains one quota like pigment bleeding through basalt rather than spawning an oasis of fresh capacity. Connection quotas and resource isolation bind each identity to a provable cost, forcing attackers to fund every forged key from the same throttled budget. Adversaries forging identities face an immediate O(k * S) capital forfeiture.
